manual: Sequential Search Algorithm Execution Process DemonstrationI. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Sequential Search Algorithm Execution Process Demonstration2. Subject: Engineering - Computer Science - Data Structures and Algorithms3. Experiment Objective: To visually demonstrate the execution process of a sequential (linear) search algorithm, understand how elements are compared one by one, and recognize the stopping condition when a target value is found.II. Experimental Materials (Virtual)1. A clean 2D animation interface.2. A horizontal array of numbered boxes, for example: [5, 1, 2, 4, 3].3. A highlighted pointer or cursor indicating the current comparison position.4. A target value to search for, for example: 4.III. Experimental Procedure1. Initialization: Display the array of numbered boxes laid out horizontally. Clearly indicate the target value to be searched.2. Pointer Placement: Place the highlighted pointer at the first element (leftmost box) of the array.3. Sequential Comparison: Move the pointer from left to right, one box at a time. At each position, highlight the current box and visually compare its value with the target value.4. Decision Process: If the current value does not match the target, visually indicate rejection (e.g., color reset) and move the pointer to the next box.5. Successful Match: When the pointer reaches the box containing the target value, highlight it distinctly and stop the pointer movement.6. Termination: Display a clear indication that the search is complete and the target has been found at the corresponding position.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Initial State: All array elements are visible, uniformly styled, and the pointer is positioned at the first element.2. During Search: The pointer moves step by step from left to right, and each visited element is highlighted in sequence.3. At Target: When the element with value 4 is reached, it remains highlighted, and the pointer stops moving.V. Summary of Experimental PrinciplesSequential search is a basic algorithm that checks each element of a list in order until the target value is found or the list ends. The core principle is direct comparison: starting from the first element, the algorithm compares each value with the target. The process guarantees correctness but may require checking all elements in the worst case. This demonstration visually maps algorithmic steps to pointer movement and highlights, making the abstract process concrete and intuitive.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Sequential (linear) search in a one-dimensional array. Minimum assumptions: a finite ordered list, a defined target value, and a pointer that inspects elements sequentially. Expected phenomena storyline: (1) array and target are presented; (2) pointer starts at the leftmost element; (3) pointer moves rightward step by step, with each element compared to the target; (4) non-matching elements are passed; (5) matching element is highlighted and motion stops. Visibility constraints: the entire array must remain visible, pointer movement must be continuous and left-to-right, and the success state must be clearly distinguishable for verification.
